data.why: The app bundles named paper analytes and retention times from Nabi et al. (2014) Programs A-C as workbench/data/paper_examples_program_a.csv and paper_examples_program_abc.csv; the analysis form defaults to 'Use named paper analytes', so no upload is required to run the demo.

goals: Run the published reference Program A/B/C calibration on named paper analytes and calculate the 51 physicochemical, environmental, and biological property estimates
Explore a property contour map and GC×GC peak map for a chosen scientific domain (environmental partitioning, biological partitioning, skin/air-blood/air-tissue, or sensory/effects)
Compare up to four properties within a scientific category to look for consistent patterns across analytes

Fit a custom instrument-transfer calibration (alpha1, alpha2, alpha3) from an uploaded n-alkane table and calibration-chemical table, then inspect calibration diagnostics (RMSE, R², extrapolation counts)
Review the model evidence, primary reference, and applicability-domain notes for a selected property before exporting results
Download wide/readable result tables and model metadata for a completed analysis

review.summary: The tree captures the tool's purpose well: turning GC×GC retention times into source-traced estimates for 51 properties, exploring them, checking calibration and applicability, and exporting. Eleven sampled screens largely back the nodes. Two of the most important paths are missing, though: analysing your own uploaded compounds and fitting a custom instrument-transfer calibration, even though the app ships example files that make a fit possible. Add those, plus a few feature corrections (tooltip claim, per-property export mapping, misplaced environmental-behaviour task), and the tree can be filed.
